title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
summary: Extending a class with extends, calling the superclass constructor with super, overriding methods and @Override, protected members, dynamic dispatch and polymorphism, the Object class with toString, equals and hashCode, casting with instanceof patterns, final, and when to prefer composition.

cards.q: `Employee e = new Manager(...); e.monthlyCost();` Which version of the overridden method runs?
cards.a:
`Manager`'s, because the actual object's class decides at run time

Dynamic dispatch picks the method of the object's real class when the program runs. The variable's type only decides which methods you may call.

cards.q: Why must `equals` and `hashCode` be overridden together?
cards.a:
Hash-based collections look up by hash code before calling `equals`

The rule is that equal objects must have equal hash codes, because a `HashSet` or `HashMap` only calls `equals` on objects in the same hash bucket. Override only `equals`, and a `HashSet` can hold two "equal" books. The compiler does not check this.

cards.q: A subclass constructor does not call `super(...)`. What happens?
cards.a:
Java calls the superclass's no-argument constructor for it

`super()` is called implicitly. If the superclass has no no-argument constructor, that is a compile error.
